author: high
claim: Plan subgoal 1 (necessity) is solved: every represented integer divisible by 3 is divisible by 9.
evidence: For F=a^3+b^3+c^3-3abc, expansion gives F=(a+b+c)Q where Q=a^2+b^2+c^2-ab-bc-ca. Since x^3-x=x(x-1)(x+1) is divisible by 3 for every integer x, F is congruent to a+b+c modulo 3. If 3|F then 3|(a+b+c). The identity Q=(a+b+c)^2-3(ab+bc+ca) then gives 3|Q. Thus each factor in F=(a+b+c)Q is divisible by 3, proving 9|F.

links.attempt_summary: Factorization plus reduction modulo 3 proves the contrapositive obstruction.

author: high
claim: Plan subgoal 2 (sufficiency) is solved: explicit nonnegative triples represent every allowed integer.
evidence: If N=3t+1 with t>=0, take (a,b,c)=(t+1,t,t), yielding F=3t+1. If N=3t+2 with t>=0, take (t,t+1,t+1), yielding F=3t+2. If N=9t with t>=1, take (t+1,t,t-1), yielding F=9t. If N=0, take (0,0,0). Direct expansion verifies each equality, and all coordinates are nonnegative.

links.attempt_summary: Three affine families cover residues 1 and 2 modulo 3 and positive multiples of 9; a separate zero triple covers N=0.

glossary.N: The nonnegative integer to be represented.
glossary.t: The integer parameter in the explicit constructions.

author: high
claim: Complete proof of the target characterization by a factorization, a modulo-3 argument, and explicit representing triples.
evidence: Define F(a,b,c)=a^3+b^3+c^3-3abc. Necessity: F=(a+b+c)Q with Q=a^2+b^2+c^2-ab-bc-ca. Since x^3 is congruent to x modulo 3, 3|F implies 3|(a+b+c); since Q=(a+b+c)^2-3(ab+bc+ca), also 3|Q, hence 9|F. Sufficiency: for t>=0, F(t+1,t,t)=3t+1 and F(t,t+1,t+1)=3t+2; for t>=1, F(t+1,t,t-1)=9t; and F(0,0,0)=0. These cover all nonnegative integers not divisible by 3 and all nonnegative multiples of 9.

subgoals: explicit construction for every allowed integer
